page: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-16 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical cores with hyperthreading enabled, running at a base clock speed of 2.3 GHz. The instance is equipped with 124 GB of system memory, yielding a high resource density of 7.75 GB of RAM per vCPU. The CPU architecture is x86_64, incorporating a 260 MB L3 cache alongside 48 KB L1d and 2 MB L2 caches per core. This instance does not include local storage or bundled GPUs, and it comes with zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data reveals strong single-core and text processing capabilities. The instance achieves a top-tier Geekbench single-core score of 2250.0 and a text processing score of 3039.0, both placing in the top 10% of tested systems. Single-threaded bzip3 decompression also reaches top-tier performance at 14.85 GB/sec. Multi-core performance is solid, with a stress-ng multi-core score of 13917.69 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 13151.0, both falling within the average range. Cryptographic and vector workloads benefit from hardware-accelerated instruction sets, including AVX-512 and Intel Advanced Matrix Extensions, which support efficient low-precision integer operations.

Memory bandwidth is measured at 1369.22 GB/sec for cached small-block reads, dropping to 111.3 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads, and 50.44 GB/sec for large-block writes. For machine learning workloads, the CPU-based LLM inference speeds reach 317.01 tokens/sec for text generation on a small 135M model, which is a strong result, while prompt processing on a medium 7B model averages 98.88 tokens/sec. A key tradeoff of this instance is the complete absence of local NVMe storage, meaning all storage operations must rely on network-attached volumes, which may limit performance for I/O-heavy database workloads despite the high memory capacity.

Given its high memory-to-vCPU ratio and dedicated compute resources, the c4-highmem-16 is qualitatively cost-efficient for workloads requiring substantial memory footprints without the overhead of excessive CPU cores. It is highly suitable for memory-intensive applications such as in-memory databases, caching layers like Redis, software compilation, and moderate-scale data processing pipelines.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4-highmem-16 is an x86_64 virtual machine instance configured with 16 dedicated vCPUs and 124 GB of RAM, providing 7.75 GB of memory per core. Powered by an Intel Xeon 8581C processor running at 2.3 GHz, it features advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 and Intel AMX for matrix operations. Benchmarks indicate top-tier single-core performance, with a Geekbench single-core score of 2250.0 and strong single-threaded compression speeds. However, multi-core benchmarks and memory write bandwidth align with average tiers. The instance lacks local storage and GPU accelerators, making network-attached storage mandatory. It is best suited for memory-intensive workloads, including in-memory databases, caching layers, software compilation, and CPU-based machine learning inference where a high memory-to-vCPU ratio is required.
